title: AI Content Checklist Before You Publish | AIVideosUGC
description: A pre-publish AI content checklist for product photos and video ads: match product details, add prices yourself, and follow platform rules. Save it now.
h1: An AI Content Checklist for Product Photos and Video Ads
lead: One wrong color, label, or extra part can turn a great-looking AI ad into a misleading one. Run this quick AI content checklist before a photo or video goes on your store, a marketplace, or an ad account, so every result matches the product customers actually receive.
summary: What to look at before an AI photo or video goes live: product accuracy, text and prices, rights, and platform labels.

sections.h2: Why a quick review is worth it
paras: An AI photo or video is a newly generated version of your product image, not a duplicate of the original photo. AI can still change a logo letter, move a button, add a piece, or shift a color.
Reviewing before you publish gives you a chance to catch product mismatches before customers see the content. The checks below work for listing photos, social posts, and paid ads alike.
sections.alt: Hands check the front pocket and zipper of the same plain black travel backpack.

sections.h2: Make sure the product matches what you ship
paras: Hold the real item, or your original photo, next to the screen and go through it piece by piece.

Color: compare the backpack in daylight, not only on a bright monitor. Shape and proportions: are the bag height, width and strap thickness right? Logos and labels: zoom in and read every letter. Parts: count pockets, straps and buckles, because the shipped bag should not gain or lose one. Size: when [a hand or a familiar object](page:tpl-size) is in the frame, does the backpack look the right size beside it?

Watch for extras as well. A [styled scene](page:lifestyle-photos) might add a candle, a plant, or a second cup. That's fine as decoration, but if a shopper could reasonably think it comes with the order, choose another version or state clearly in the listing what's included.
sections.alt: Hands count pockets, buckles and straps on the same plain black travel backpack.

paras: Play the clip full screen on your phone, the way most people will see it, then go through it slowly. Movement is where [AI video](page:video-hub) tends to slip: the black backpack label area can blur as it turns, fingers can blend into a strap, or a zipper can change shape halfway through.
Look closely at the hands holding the black backpack. Count fingers and watch how they grip the straps, open the zipper or turn the bag over.

Give extra attention to the first frame, since it often becomes the thumbnail. If one short backpack moment is off, trim around it in CapCut; if the problem runs through the whole clip, make a new version.
sections.alt: Hands open the zipper and flap of the same plain black travel backpack.

sections.h2: Put words, prices, and offers on last
paras: Don't ask the AI to write your price, launch date, discount code, or headline into the picture. Generated lettering is often misspelled or garbled. Make the visual first, then add text in Canva, CapCut, or Ads Manager, where you control every character.

Before posting, check that the price and code on the ad match your store exactly and that any end date hasn't already passed. Then scan the generated image for stray letters on packaging or signs in the background. If you spot any, crop them out or try again.
sections.alt: Hands hold the same plain black travel backpack beside a blank phone.

sections.h2: Own or license everything that appears
paras: Upload only product photos you took yourself or have the rights to use. If you're working from a supplier's photo, make sure your agreement with them covers using it in ads. Feature only logos and trademarks that belong to you. Requests built around another company's marks may be refused, and so may anything involving celebrities or other public figures. Our [Content Policy](/content) and [Trust and Safety](page:trust) pages explain what can be uploaded and how reports are handled.
The same applies to what you add later. Pick music from the commercial-use library in your editing app or ad platform, or a track you've licensed for advertising, rather than a song you simply like.
sections.alt: Hands hold the same plain black travel backpack beside a plain camera and blank phone.

sections.h2: Follow each platform's current rules on AI content
paras: Several platforms ask creators and advertisers to mark realistic AI-generated people or scenes, and some offer a toggle or tag for it when you post. The rules differ between platforms and get updated, so read the current policy on each site you use instead of relying on an old screenshot or a forum thread.

Two habits help wherever you post. Don't present an [AI-generated person](page:model-photos) as a real customer or reviewer. And don't let a caption promise health, skin, or weight results; show how the product is used and leave the conclusions to the shopper.
sections.alt: Hands check the first frame of the same plain black travel backpack beside blank devices.

checklist: Color, shape, logos, and part count match the real product
No prop could be mistaken for something included in the order
The video holds together from first frame to last, with no warping
Prices, codes, and dates were added by you and match your store
Every photo, logo, and music track is yours or licensed for ads
Each platform's current AI labeling rules have been read and followed

faq.q: What should I check before posting an AI-made video?
faq.a: Watch it all the way through and compare the product with the real item: shape, color, parts and any label. Make sure every action is something your product really does and that no stray text or logos appear.

faq.q: What if only one small detail is wrong?
faq.a: Make another version rather than posting it. A wrong button or color can mislead buyers, and each new version shows its credit cost before it starts.

faq.q: Can I publish a result with a small label error?
faq.a: No. Generate another version or use a real label photo. A wrong ingredient, size, color, or safety statement can mislead buyers.

faq.q: Does a 30-second video need the same review as a shorter clip?
faq.a: Yes. Review the full 30-second video from first frame to last, just as you would a 6, 10 or 15-second clip. Longer footage gives more moments for a label or hand to warp.

faq.q: How many credits does a review version use?
faq.a: A 6-second version uses 24 credits, a 10-second version uses 40, a 15-second version uses 60 and a 30-second version uses 120. You see the cost before each new version starts.

faq.q: Can an AI-generated person give a customer testimonial?
faq.a: No. Do not present an AI-generated person as a customer or reviewer. Keep the claim tied to the product and add the disclosure required by the platform where you post.

steps_h2: How to Review AI Product Content in 3 Simple Steps
steps_lead: Check one backpack from source photo to final frame before you publish the result.

steps.d: Put the original black backpack or its source photo beside the generated result and compare shape, color, parts and label area. You catch mismatches before a shopper sees them.
Watch the black backpack move, then check every price, claim and added caption in your editor. You can correct warped motion and wording before the ad runs.
Download the reviewed backpack image or clip only after it matches the item you ship. Add your approved offer and platform disclosure, then publish it where your buyers will see it.

cta_title: Check every product detail before your next ad
cta_lead: Upload a product photo, review the generated result against the item you ship and download only the version you can stand behind.
